stem: Input EC is stable, but root-zone EC rises as containers are allowed to dry much more deeply between irrigations. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: The fertilizer concentrate must have changed even though input EC is stable
Lower root-zone water content can concentrate dissolved ions, so irrigation pattern and salt accumulation should be evaluated together
The EC increase proves root disease
Root-zone EC cannot change unless source-water pH changes
rationale: As root-zone water content declines, dissolved ions can become more concentrated. EC trends should therefore be interpreted together with moisture status and irrigation behavior.
